hints.text: Look at each term on its own. Both are perfect squares, and they are joined by a minus sign.
Use the difference of squares pattern $a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b)$ with $a = x$ and $b = 5$, since $25 = 5^2$.
Putting $x$ and $5$ into the pattern gives the factored form $(x + 5)(x - 5)$.

explanation: Both terms are perfect squares with a minus sign between them, because $25 = 5^2$. This is a difference of squares.
The pattern is $a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b)$, and here $a = x$ and $b = 5$.
Substituting into the pattern gives the factored form $x^2 - 25 = (x + 5)(x - 5)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why the middle vanishes
steps: They are perfect opposites, so they cancel to zero.
Left over: x² − 25 — that is why the factored form has a plus AND a minus.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two-number hunt still works
steps: Think of x² − 25 as x² + 0x − 25: numbers multiplying to −25 and adding to 0.
